response.passage: Rohan is designing a layout for his new stationery shop on a large grid map. He marks the main entrance at the origin, which is the point (0, 0), where both the horizontal and vertical measurements begin. To ensure accuracy, Rohan uses a uniform scale where every grid square represents exactly one meter on both axes. He places the pen display at point (3, 0) to be easily accessible from the entrance. Because this point lies directly on the horizontal line, it is not inside any quadrant. Rohan then places the notebook shelf at (2, 5) and the art supplies at (5, 2). He carefully distinguishes between these two locations because the first number represents the horizontal distance from the entrance, while the second number represents the vertical distance. Finally, he calculates the distance between the entrance (0, 0) and the pen display (3, 0) using the square root of the sum of squared differences, ensuring his measurements are precise for the floor plan.
response.summary: Rohan uses a coordinate grid to map out his stationery shop layout. He ensures consistent scaling and precise placement of items to distinguish between different locations on the floor.
